summary.summary_text: Nations Trust Bank is a licensed commercial bank serving corporate, commercial, and consumer customers in Sri Lanka through 96 branches plus digital channels (Annual Report 2023, p.4). It earns money primarily through net interest margin on loans/deposits (spread x book), plus fee and commission income and trading gains -- net interest income was LKR 38.5Bn of LKR 52.2Bn total operating income in FY2025 (Annual Report 2025, p.151). As a bank, its profile is bound by CBSL regulation (capital adequacy, liquidity coverage) rather than a product-market dependency in the usual sense. Group profit after tax grew from LKR 4.1Bn (FY2020) to LKR 19.3Bn (FY2025), roughly 4.7x, with the sharpest single jump in FY2023 (+59%) following Sri Lanka's 2022 default and subsequent rate cycle, and Return on Equity peaking at 24.2% in FY2024 before easing to 21.9% in FY2025 as competitive and margin pressure returned (Performance Highlights, Annual Reports 2021/2023/2025).
summary.gaps_note: No gaps for FY2020-FY2025 and the latest interim; all figures traced to each report's own 'Performance Highlights' summary table, cross-checked against the audited Statement of Profit or Loss where read.

financials_interim.notes: Group basis. Gross Income Rs 21,927,226k, PAT Rs 6,117,997k, Basic EPS Rs 18.50 for the quarter ended 30 Sept 2025 (Income Statement, Quarter ended 30 September column).
COMPANY (Bank standalone) basis. EPS 51.49 = 17,166,738k/333,426,766 confirmed exactly. See GROUP row's notes for shared HSBC-acquisition and extraction detail.

Nations Trust Bank PLC, a licensed commercial bank (FYE 31 December). MAJOR CAVEAT FOR THIS PERIOD: on 1 May 2026 the Group completed the acquisition of HSBC Sri Lanka's retail banking business (loans incl. credit cards, deposits, workforce, branch leases) for cash consideration of Rs.21,784,615k, recognised as a business combination under SLFRS 3 with provisional goodwill of Rs.22,190,416k -- this makes YoY comparisons NOT like-for-like: the acquisition drove ~32% of the Group's asset growth and is explicitly the reason the prior INTERIM_REPORT entry for NTB (Q3 FY2025, quarter ended 30 Sept 2025, a stale stub with no narrative) was superseded rather than extended with QoQ, since the business itself changed materially mid-period. A prior financial_statements row for NTB existed at period_end_date 2025-09-30 (GROUP basis only, no COMPANY row, no interim_updates) -- left untouched; this new entry is for period_end_date 2026-06-30 and should be treated as effectively the first meaningful entry for this symbol given the stale/incomplete prior row. This entry uses the filing's 6-MONTH CUMULATIVE (H1, six months ended 30 June 2026) figures, consistent with SAMP and CBNK entered this session; the filing also separately gives quarter-only columns (not used here, though referenced in the narrative for color, since management's own press release explicitly breaks out Q1 vs Q2). Mapped per bank convention: revenue = 'Total Operating Income'; operating_profit = 'Operating profit/(loss) before VAT & SSCL on financial services', the Bank's own subtotal. finance_costs/finance_income left blank -- interest expense already netted into revenue via Net Interest Income. VAT+SSCL on financial services (Rs.3,924mn Bank H1 2026) is not a separate stored field; profit_before_tax stored here is AFTER this levy, matching the filing's own 'Profit before Income Tax' line. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per bank convention. short_term_borrowings = 'Due to Banks' + 'Due to debt securities holders - Repurchase Agreements' (both short-tenor by nature); long_term_borrowings = 'Due to Other Borrowers' + 'Debt Securities Issued'. 'Due to Depositors' (Rs.688,914,454k Bank / Rs.687,953,741k Group) deliberately excluded -- deposit funding, not debt. shares_in_issue = voting (288,491,548) + non-voting (44,935,218) = 333,426,766, cross-checked against EPS: 17,166,738k/333,426,766=51.49 Bank, exact match to disclosed 51.49 -- confirms this share count is correct (small variance from a pure weighted-average calc is expected/immaterial). The income tax line swung from a genuine EXPENSE (Rs.4,789,137k Bank H1 2025) to a CREDIT (Rs.1,164,075k Bank H1 2026) -- stored as tax_expense=-1164075 (negative, i.e. a credit) per the accounting-identity convention used elsewhere in this project (PBT - tax_expense = PAT holds with this sign). No column-swap issues found -- every subtotal ties exactly across Bank/Group and six-month/quarter columns.

thesis.thesis_text: Nations Trust Bank is a mid-tier Sri Lankan commercial bank with 90 branches and a corporate/commercial/consumer mix. FY2025 Group PAT grew 14.6% to LKR 19.3bn on 17.6% growth in total operating income, while the loan book expanded nearly 50% YoY -- strong growth, though rapid balance-sheet expansion in a bank always warrants watching for asset-quality slippage a few years out. At 5.4x trailing P/E and 0.93x P/B, the stock is statistically cheap, but this project has no way to separate an NTB-specific discount from a sector-wide Sri Lankan banking discount without peer comparisons not yet built (Annual Report FY2025, p.151-152).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no CBSL/IMF/World Bank/news data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Governance & Risk is also necessarily thin -- no circulars/disclosures feed exists (deliberately disabled this session), so insider transactions, board changes, and rights issues cannot be verified directly; the score below reflects only what's visible in audited financial statements and public market data.

financial_quality.rationale: FY2025 Group ROE 19.9%, ROA 2.75% -- solid returns for a commercial bank. Current ratio/debt-equity are not meaningful for a bank's balance sheet structure and are correctly left blank rather than forced. Total assets grew 28.4% YoY, a rapid pace worth monitoring for asset-quality risk though not yet a red flag.

growth_outlook.rationale: Total operating income (revenue proxy) +17.6% YoY, PAT +14.6% YoY (16.8bn to 19.3bn), loan book (Financial Assets at Amortised Cost - Loans and Advances) up from 287bn to 430bn, +49.8% YoY -- aggressive balance-sheet growth alongside earnings growth.

valuation.rationale: P/E 5.4x and P/B 0.93x are statistically cheap, though this likely reflects a Sri Lanka banking-sector-wide sovereign-risk discount rather than an NTB-specific issue -- can't fully separate the two without peer bank comparisons not yet built. Dividend yield 2.25% with a low 12.1% payout (capital retention, likely for growth/regulatory buffers).

business_quality.rationale: Established mid-tier commercial bank (90 branches, digital channels, A(lka) credit rating) with corporate/commercial/consumer mix -- solid franchise, but bank quality is inseparable from Sri Lanka's broader macro/sovereign risk, which this project cannot independently assess (no macro data source).

governance_risk.rationale: Heavily regulated by CBSL by nature of being a licensed bank (a governance positive), explicit A(lka) credit rating disclosed. No disclosures feed to verify recent board/ownership changes.

key_reasons: PAT growth of 14.6% YoY on 17.6% revenue growth, with ROE near 20%
P/E of 5.4x and P/B of 0.93x are statistically cheap versus the pilot set
4 periods of financials on file including a genuine quarterly interim -- among the best-covered pilots
watch_factors: Loan book grew ~50% YoY -- rapid credit growth is a leading indicator worth monitoring for future asset-quality risk, not yet a problem in the data on file
Low 12.1% payout ratio suggests capital is being retained, possibly for regulatory buffers or continued loan growth -- not yet flagged as a concern but worth tracking
Cheap multiples may reflect Sri Lanka banking-sector risk rather than an NTB-specific opportunity -- no peer-bank comparison built yet to test this

horizon_notes.6m: Q1 FY2026 interim results (once filed) will show whether the ~50% loan growth pace continues or moderates.
horizon_notes.1y: If asset quality holds up under this growth pace, the cheap P/E and P/B could re-rate; if not, provisions could pressure PAT.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on whether NTB can convert rapid loan growth into sustained, well-provisioned earnings without a credit-cycle setback.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/rate-cycle data source in this project to assess how a multi-year Sri Lankan rate cycle would affect NTB's net interest margin.

interim_updates.note_text: Nations Trust Bank's results for H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026) are dominated by a single event: on 1 May 2026 the Group completed the acquisition of HSBC Sri Lanka's retail banking business (loans including credit cards, deposits, workforce and branch leases) for Rs.21.78bn cash, recognised as a business combination with provisional goodwill of Rs.22.19bn -- this is NOT a like-for-like YoY comparison. Group Total Operating Income grew 18.8% YoY to Rs.30.35bn, with Net Interest Income +16.7% (Rs.19.04bn to Rs.22.22bn) and Net Fee & Commission Income +23.1% (Rs.4.10bn to Rs.5.04bn) -- both genuine core-business growth even before the acquisition's contribution (which only entered from 1 May, two months of the six-month period). Group PBT grew a much more modest 6.0% (Rs.13.67bn to Rs.14.48bn) as impairment charges rose sharply (+282% per the filing's own change column) and operating expenses grew ~26%. The headline PAT growth of 77.0% (Rs.8.79bn to Rs.15.56bn) is substantially inflated by a ONE-OFF TAX CREDIT tied to the acquisition: the Group's income tax line swung from a genuine expense of Rs.4.88bn in H1 2025 to a credit of Rs.1.08bn in H1 2026, a swing of Rs.5.95bn that alone accounts for roughly 88% of the Rs.6.77bn increase in Group PAT (and, at the standalone Bank level, a Rs.5.95bn tax swing accounts for ~69% of the Rs.8.58bn PAT increase). Per management's own press release, Q1 2026 PAT (pre-acquisition) was approximately Rs.4.6bn Group, with the balance of H1 profit generated in Q2 as the acquisition completed and its one-off tax benefit was recognised. Return on Equity rose to 31.33% (Group) from 21.86%, reflecting both the earnings jump and the acquisition's impact on the balance sheet; Net Interest Margin was broadly stable at 5.58% (Bank) versus 6.05% at year-end 2025 (a full-year reference point, not directly comparable to the H1 2025 period).
interim_updates.gaps_note: A prior financial_statements row exists for NTB at period_end_date 2025-09-30 (GROUP basis, quarter ended 30 September 2025) but has no interim_updates narrative and predates the HSBC acquisition -- given the acquisition makes this period structurally non-comparable to any prior quarter (the Group's asset base and business composition changed materially on 1 May 2026), no QoQ comparison was attempted against that stale row; this entry is treated as the first substantive entry for NTB. This entry uses the filing's 6-MONTH CUMULATIVE (H1) figures rather than a discrete quarter, consistent with SAMP and CBNK entered this session; the filing's own quarter-only columns exist but were not used as the primary stored figures (referenced qualitatively in the narrative only).
interim_updates.takeaway: The core banking business grew genuinely well (NII +17%, fees +23%), but the 77% PAT growth headline is mostly a tax-credit artefact tied to the HSBC acquisition accounting, not underlying earnings power -- a Rs.5.95bn swing in the tax line alone explains roughly 88% of the Group's PAT increase. The acquisition itself (completed 1 May 2026, ~Rs.21.8bn cash, provisional goodwill of Rs.22.2bn) is a genuine strategic step-change for the Bank's scale and market position in retail/credit cards, but its full run-rate P&L contribution is not yet visible in this two-month partial period, and the purchase price allocation (including the split between goodwill and identifiable intangibles) remains provisional, subject to change within a 12-month measurement period.
operational_highlights: Group Total Operating Income +18.8% YoY to Rs.30.35bn; Net Interest Income +16.7% to Rs.22.22bn; Net Fee & Commission Income +23.1% to Rs.5.04bn

1 May 2026: Group completed acquisition of HSBC Sri Lanka's retail banking business for Rs.21.78bn cash -- provisional goodwill of Rs.22.19bn recognised; loans/deposits/workforce/branch leases transferred
Group PBT +6.0% YoY to Rs.14.48bn, a much smaller increase than revenue growth, as impairment charges rose 282% and operating expenses grew ~26%

Group PAT +77.0% YoY to Rs.15.56bn -- but the income tax line swung from a Rs.4.88bn expense to a Rs.1.08bn credit (a Rs.5.95bn swing), which alone explains ~88% of the PAT increase; this is a one-off tax benefit tied to the acquisition, not recurring operating strength
Return on Equity rose to 31.33% (Group) from 21.86% a year earlier; Net Interest Margin 5.58% (Bank), broadly stable vs the 6.05% year-end-2025 reference

Per management's press release, Q1 2026 (pre-acquisition) Group PAT was ~Rs.4.6bn, with the balance of the H1 profit -- including the acquisition's initial contribution and the one-off tax credit -- recognised in Q2
key_drivers: The HSBC Sri Lanka retail banking acquisition (completed 1 May 2026, Rs.21.78bn cash consideration, Rs.22.19bn provisional goodwill) is the single dominant event of the period -- it drove much of the balance-sheet growth (Total Assets +31.8% Bank YoY) but its P&L contribution reflects only two months of the six-month period and remains provisional pending SLFRS 3 purchase price allocation

A Rs.5.95bn swing in the income tax line (from a Rs.4.88bn expense to a Rs.1.08bn credit, Group) is the single largest driver of the 77% PAT growth headline -- explicitly a one-off item tied to the acquisition, not organic earnings growth
Impairment charges rose 282% YoY per the filing's own disclosure, a genuine cost the acquisition-driven PAT growth narrative should not obscure
Net Interest Income (+16.7%) and Net Fee & Commission Income (+23.1%) growth both predate and are separate from the acquisition's contribution, and represent genuine core-business momentum
